content.value_statement: Modern JavaScript projects need fast tests that match Vite workflows. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Vitest setup, mocks, coverage, fixtures, filtering, snapshots, and CI usage.
actual_capabilities: Explains Vitest configuration, CLI commands, watch mode, and CI run mode.
Shows how to structure tests with test, describe, hooks, and expect assertions.
Guides mocking for modules, functions, timers, globals, and environment variables.
Covers snapshots, coverage providers, thresholds, and update workflows.
Documents fixtures, projects, filtering, concurrency, sharding, and type testing.
limitations: The guidance is based on Vitest 3.x content generated on 2026-01-28.
It cannot verify your installed Vitest version without repository access.
It does not replace official release notes for new Vitest behavior.
It focuses on Vitest and does not provide full end-to-end test framework guidance.

use_cases.title: Create Unit Tests
use_cases.description: Write Vitest tests for functions, components, async behavior, and error paths using Jest-compatible patterns.

use_cases.title: Maintain Library Quality
use_cases.description: Add type tests, snapshots, fixtures, and coverage thresholds for reusable JavaScript or TypeScript packages.

use_cases.title: Tune CI Test Runs
use_cases.description: Configure run mode, sharding, filtering, project selection, reporters, and coverage output for continuous integration.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Vitest Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Vitest skill to write tests for my module. Include normal cases, edge cases, and async behavior when relevant.

prompt_templates.title: Add Mocks and Spies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Vitest skill to mock external modules, spy on object methods, and restore mocks after each test.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Coverage and CI
prompt_templates.scenario: Project setup for repeatable automated checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Vitest skill to configure coverage, reporters, watch behavior, and CI-friendly test scripts for this repository.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Project Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Vitest skill to plan projects, fixtures, sharding, filtering, type tests, snapshots, and environment settings for a monorepo.

output_examples.input: A user asks for Vitest tests for a TypeScript utility.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes focused test cases, assertion choices, setup notes, and edge cases without changing unrelated files.

output_examples.input: A user needs mocking guidance for an API client.
output: Explains when to use module mocks, spies, and manual mocks.
Identifies cleanup steps to prevent state from leaking between tests.
Suggests assertions that verify behavior without reaching the network.

output_examples.input: A team wants Vitest in CI with coverage.
output_examples.output: The assistant outlines run mode, reporter selection, coverage provider choices, thresholds, sharding, and snapshot update cautions.

best_practices: Use project-local Vitest configuration and keep test options close to the code under test.
Restore mocks, timers, globals, and environment stubs after tests that mutate shared state.
Run focused filters locally, then run the full suite in CI before merging changes.
anti_patterns: Do not leave focused tests or skipped tests in committed code without a clear reason.
Do not update snapshots blindly when a behavior change is not understood.
Do not use real services or real secrets in unit tests that should rely on mocks.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create and maintain Vitest tests, configuration, mocks, snapshots, coverage, fixtures, filtering, and CI workflows.

faq.question: Can it convert Jest tests to Vitest?
faq.answer: It can guide common Jest-compatible patterns and note Vitest differences, but project-specific migration still needs review.

faq.question: Does it run my tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance. Test execution depends on the host tool and repository permissions.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The references cover TypeScript, type testing, expectTypeOf, and Vitest configuration for typed projects.

faq.question: Can it help with browser-like tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers jsdom, happy-dom, environment options, and custom environments for Vitest test suites.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with secrets?
faq.answer: Avoid real secrets in tests. Use stubs or placeholders for environment values and restore them after each test.
